sub_answers.text: The Local Government Act 1972 created a two-tier system of metropolitan counties and districts covering Tyne and Wear, of which Newcastle was a district [d67582869s1p0]. The Local Government Act 1985 abolished the metropolitan counties and transferred most powers to the metropolitan districts, which took on county-level functions as metropolitan boroughs [d67582869s1p0]. Since 1986 some councils have provided both district-level and county-level functions, sometimes through joint arrangements with other Tyne and Wear councils [d41381311s2p0]. The North of Tyne Combined Authority was created in 2018 and was given strategic powers covering a region overlapping the former Tyne and Wear county and Northumberland, representing a regional statutory layer above individual councils [d67582869s1p0]. In 2024 a wider North East Mayoral Combined Authority was established, chaired by a directly elected mayor and overseeing delivery of certain strategic functions across multiple councils including Newcastle, creating additional statutory limits on individual council autonomy for those strategic areas [d41381311s2p0].
